title: Nine Days to the World Cup. For NRIs in North America, the Party Is Finally in Their Backyard.
excerpt: The 2026 FIFA World Cup kicks off June 11 across the US, Canada, and Mexico — home to over five million Indians. No 3 AM alarms. No grainy streams. This time, they can drive to the stadium.
body:
The FIFA World Cup has never been closer to the Indian diaspora — literally.

When the tournament kicks off on **June 11** across the **United States, Canada, and Mexico**, it will be the first time in history that the world's biggest sporting event is hosted entirely in countries where millions of Indians have made their homes. The three host nations are home to an estimated **five million people of Indian origin**, concentrated in cities that will stage some of the tournament's most high-profile matches.

## The Broadcast Drama Is Over

For weeks, Indian football fans — both in India and abroad — had braced for the possibility of having no legal way to watch the World Cup on television. FIFA's asking price of $100 million for Indian broadcast rights went begging. JioStar, the Reliance-Disney joint venture that aired the 2022 tournament, reportedly offered $20 million. Sony, which held rights for the 2014 and 2018 editions, held talks but never formally bid.

Then, on June 1, **Zee Entertainment** stepped in. The deal, covering the 2026 World Cup and 38 other FIFA events through 2034, was announced just ten days before kickoff. Matches will air on **Unite8 Sports** (Zee's sports channels) and stream on **Zee5**. Financial terms were not disclosed, though Reuters had previously reported FIFA slashed its asking price to $60 million.

In the US and Canada, all 104 matches will air on **Fox** and **FS1**, with Spanish-language coverage on **Telemundo** and **Peacock**.

## Where NRIs Can Watch — and Attend

For Indian-Americans in the New York-New Jersey metro area, the tournament's crown jewel is at their doorstep: the **final on July 19** at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The semifinal on July 15 is at the same venue.

Other key host cities with large Indian populations include:

- **Houston** (NRG Stadium) — one of the largest Indian communities in the US, with prominent temples, restaurants, and community organizations along the Hillcroft corridor
- **Dallas** (AT&T Stadium) — rapidly growing Indian population in the DFW suburbs
- **San Francisco Bay Area** (Levi's Stadium, Santa Clara) — home to hundreds of thousands of Indian tech professionals
- **Seattle** (Lumen Field) — strong Indian presence in the tech corridor
- **Toronto** (BMO Field) — Canada's largest Indian community, over 800,000 strong
- **Vancouver** (BC Place) — deep Punjabi and South Asian roots

## The Groups That Matter to NRI Fans

While India has never qualified for the World Cup, diaspora fans typically rally behind adopted countries, ancestral rivals, and football's global stars. The key groups for NRI interest:

**Group D** features the **United States** — home team for millions of Indian-Americans — alongside Paraguay, Australia, and Turkey. The USMNT's World Cup campaign will be the most-watched sporting event in the country this summer.

**Group L** has **England**, historically popular among cricket-watching Indians. They face Croatia, Ghana, and Panama.

**Group J** features **Argentina** with **Lionel Messi** — potentially in his final World Cup. The 38-year-old was named to the squad but may not start every match. NRI football fans across North America have tracked Messi since his Inter Miami move in 2023.

**Group F** includes **Japan**, increasingly popular among younger Indian fans, and the **Netherlands**.

## Key Dates to Mark

- **June 11** — Tournament opens: Mexico vs. South Africa (Group A) at Estadio Azteca, Mexico City
- **June 14** — USA's first match vs. Paraguay (Group D)
- **June 27** — Group stage ends
- **July 4-7** — Round of 16
- **July 19** — Final at MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford, NJ

## The Scale of Indian Interest

India may not have a team in the tournament, but it is one of football's biggest television markets. During the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, India accounted for **2.9 percent of the global linear television audience** — second only to China. An estimated 745 million viewers watched across TV and digital platforms, with television viewership alone reaching nearly 84 million.

Those numbers explain why FIFA held firm on pricing for so long. For diaspora fans in North America, though, the numbers that matter are simpler: a 90-minute drive to the stadium, a weeknight match that kicks off at 7 PM instead of 3 AM, and a summer where the world's game is, for once, on their time zone.

*The 2026 FIFA World Cup runs June 11 to July 19 across 16 venues in the United States, Canada, and Mexico.*
author: Diaspora Desk
